subject: chemistry-2
question: Which comparison between a strong acid and a weak acid prepared at the same molar concentration is accurate?

options.text: The strong acid has the higher pH because it holds its protons tightly
Both solutions have the same hydronium concentration because molarity sets pH
The weak acid ionizes completely but neutralizes added base more slowly
The strong acid ionizes essentially completely, so it has the lower pH

explanation:
Acid strength describes the extent of ionization, not the amount of acid dissolved. A strong acid such as HCl dissociates essentially completely, releasing far more hydronium per mole than a weak acid such as acetic acid, which establishes an equilibrium with most molecules still undissociated. More hydronium means a lower pH, so at equal molarity the strong acid gives the more acidic solution.

ELI-10: Concentration counts how much acid you added; strength counts what fraction of it actually lets go of its proton. In 0.1 mol/L HCl essentially every molecule releases H+, giving about 0.1 mol/L hydronium and a pH near 1. In 0.1 mol/L acetic acid only about 1 percent releases H+, giving roughly 0.001 mol/L and a pH near 3. Same amount dissolved, about a hundredfold difference in hydronium.
source: OpenStax — Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e); NIST — Reference Data / Constants (https://www.nist.gov/pml)
